original_value: A novel global harmony search (NGHS) algorithm, as proposed in 2010, is an improved algorithm that combines the harmony search (HS), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and a genetic algorithm (GA). Moreover, the fixed parameter of mutation probability was used in the NGHS algorithm. However, appropriate parameters can enhance the searching ability of a metaheuristic algorithm, and their importance has been described in many studies. Inspired by the adjustment strategy of the improved harmony search (IHS) algorithm, a dynamic adjusting novel global harmony search (DANGHS) algorithm, which combines NGHS and dynamic adjustment strategies for genetic mutation probability, is introduced in this paper. Moreover, extensive computational experiments and comparisons are carried out for 14 benchmark continuous optimization problems. The results show that the proposed DANGHS algorithm has better performance in comparison with other HS algorithms in most problems. In addition, the proposed algorithm is more efficient than previous methods. Finally, different strategies are suitable for different situations. Among these strategies, the most interesting and exciting strategy is the periodic dynamic adjustment strategy. For a specific problem, the periodic dynamic adjustment strategy could have better performance in comparison with other decreasing or increasing strategies. These results inspire us to further investigate this kind of periodic dynamic adjustment strategy in future experiments.

result.paraphrase: A novel global harmony search (NGHS) algorithm, introduced in 2010, is an enhanced method that integrates harmony search (HS), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and a genetic algorithm (GA). In NGHS, the mutation probability is kept fixed. Since suitable parameter settings can improve the search capability of a metaheuristic algorithm, and many studies have highlighted their importance, this paper presents a dynamic adjusting novel global harmony search (DANGHS) algorithm inspired by the adjustment strategy of the improved harmony search (IHS) algorithm. DANGHS combines NGHS with dynamic adjustment strategies for genetic mutation probability. Extensive computational experiments and comparisons were performed on 14 benchmark continuous optimization problems. The results indicate that the proposed DANGHS algorithm outperforms other HS algorithms on most problems. It is also more efficient than earlier methods. Finally, different strategies are appropriate for different situations. Of these, the periodic dynamic adjustment strategy is the most interesting and promising. For a specific problem, it may perform better than other decreasing or increasing strategies. These findings motivate further study of this periodic dynamic adjustment strategy in future experiments.
